==Problem==
In a sequence of positive integers, each term after the second is the product of the previous two terms. The sixth term is <imath>4000</imath>. What is the first term?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 1 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 2 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 4 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 5 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 10</imath>

==Solution 1==
In this solution, we will use trial and error to solve.
<imath>4000</imath> can be expressed as <imath>200 \times 20</imath>. We divide <imath>200</imath> by <imath>20</imath> and get <imath>10</imath>, divide <imath>20</imath> by <imath>10</imath> and get <imath>2</imath>, and divide <imath>10</imath> by <imath>2</imath> to get <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 5}</imath>. No one said that they have to be in ascending order!

Solution by [[User:ILoveMath31415926535|ILoveMath31415926535]] and clarification edits by apex304

==Solution 2==
Consider the first term is <imath>A</imath> and the second term is <imath>B</imath>. Then, the following terms will be <imath>AB</imath>, <imath>AB^2</imath>, <imath>A^2B^3</imath> and <imath>A^3B^5</imath>. Notice that <imath>4000=2^5\times 5^3</imath>, then we obtain <imath>A=\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 5}</imath> and <imath>B=2</imath>. 

Solution by Slimeknight, edited by XingZheZhong
